text:
1	# LOOM portal: interface for agents
2	
3	This page is for an agent (or the developer of one) that needs part of a
4	person's health context to do a task for them. It is the only document an
5	agent needs; it does not have to read LOOM's source.
6	
7	## What LOOM offers
8	
9	LOOM holds one person's health record and hands out **task-scoped,
10	expiring slices** of it. You say what task you are doing; LOOM decides
11	how deep you may see, which fields you get, and for how long.
12	
13	| Tier | What it contains | Field names |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| L0 | raw sensor signal | `raw_signal` |
16	| L1 | readings (here: hourly glucose, mg/dL) | `readings` |
17	| L2 | patterns and alerts derived from readings | `glucose_patterns`, `alerts` |
18	| L3 | plain-language constraints | `constraints` |
19	
20	L0 is the deepest (most revealing), L3 the shallowest. A tier includes the
21	shallower ones: an L2 grant may carry `constraints` too.
22	
23	## Access
24	
25	- Base URL and namespace are given to you by whoever runs the portal (for
26	  a test: `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and a namespace such as `demo`).
27	  Every call for one person goes to `/v1/<namespace>/...`.
28	- There is no login in v0.1. You identify yourself with `agent_id` (this
29	  agent instance) and `publisher` (the company or developer that ships
30	  it). In Nanda Town the gateway fills `agent_id` from the signed envelope;
31	  over plain HTTP both are claims.
32	- JSON in, JSON out. Errors are JSON `{"error": "..."}`; a malformed body
33	  gets HTTP 400 naming the missing fields.
34	
35	## Endpoints
36	
37	| Method and path | Use |
38	|---|---|
39	| `GET /health` | version and policy id |
40	| `POST /v1/<ns>/requests` | ask for access for a task; a grant carries data immediately |
41	| `POST /v1/<ns>/fetch` | get fresh data again under a grant you already hold |
42	| `GET /v1/<ns>/credit` | publisher → credit score (only publishers that have been seen) |
43	| `GET /v1/<ns>/log` | the person's audit log: every decision, without the data (owner token only; agents get 403) |
44	| `GET /v1/policy` | the built-in tasks, as JSON (same as the table below) |
45	| `GET /v1/<ns>/proposals/<proposal_id>` | status of a proposal for a task that is not built in (see below) |
46	
47	### `POST /v1/<ns>/requests`: body
48	
49	| Field | Required | Meaning |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| `request_id` | yes | unique per request; reuse it only to retry the same request |
52	| `agent_id` | yes | your agent instance |
53	| `publisher` | yes | who ships you |
54	| `category` | yes | `agent_for_user` (works for the person) or `care_provider` (clinician side) |
55	| `task` | yes | one of the task names below |
56	| `purpose` | no | free text, recorded |
57	| `tier` | yes | the deepest tier you ask for (`L0`..`L3`) |
58	| `fields` | yes | list of field names you ask for |
59	| `at` | yes | current time on the person's timeline, in days (number) |
60	
61	### Tasks (policy `loom-policy-0.2.1`)
62	
63	| `task` | `category` | Deep

mkdir -p /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out && cat > /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out/grocer-1.md <<'EOF'
# This week's grocery list (grocer-1, freshcart), day 0

**Status: draft. Please confirm before I act on it.** LOOM marked this as a first request from freshcart, so nothing gets ordered or sent anywhere until you OK it.

Built around two health constraints from your LOOM record: **limit added sugar** and **prefer low-glycemic foods**. Amounts assume one person eating most meals at home for 7 days. Adjust as you like.

## Produce
- Leafy greens: spinach (1 large bag), mixed salad greens (1 box)
- Broccoli (2 heads), cauliflower (1 head)
- Bell peppers (4), zucchini (2), cucumbers (2)
- Cherry tomatoes (1 pint), onions (3), garlic (1 bulb)
- Mushrooms (8 oz)
- Avocados (3)
- Berries: blueberries and raspberries (1 pint each). Lower-glycemic fruit
- Apples (3), pears (2). Whole fruit rather than juice
- Lemons (2)

## Protein
- Eggs (1 dozen)
- Chicken breast or thighs (~1.5 lb)
- Salmon fillets (2)
- Firm tofu (1 block)
- Canned tuna or sardines in water/olive oil (2 cans)

## Dairy and alternatives
- Plain unsweetened Greek yogurt (32 oz). Sweeten with berries, not flavored cups
- Unsweetened almond or soy milk, or regular milk (half gallon)
- Cheese: feta or a block of cheddar (small)

## Whole grains and legumes (low-glycemic carbs)
- Steel-cut or rolled oats (not instant flavored packets)
- Quinoa (1 bag)
- Brown rice or farro (1 bag)
- 100% whole-grain or sprouted bread (1 loaf, check label for added sugar)
- Lentils, dry (1 lb)
- Canned chickpeas and black beans (2 cans each, low-sodium)

## Pantry
- Extra-virgin olive oil
- Nuts: almonds and walnuts (unsalted, ~8 oz each)
- Chia or ground flax seeds
- Natural peanut or almond butter (ingredients: nuts, maybe salt, no added sugar)
- Canned crushed tomatoes (no sugar added)
- Spices: cinnamon, cumin, paprika, black pepper
- Plain or sparkling water, unsweetened tea/coffee

## Snacks
- Hummus (1 tub)
- Baby carrots, celery
- Plain popcorn kernels or air-popped popcorn
- Dark chocolate, 85%+ (small bar, optional)

## Skipped or swapped this week
- Soda, juice, sweetened teas → sparkling water, unsweetened tea
- Flavored yogurt → plain Greek yogurt + berries
- Sugary cereal, granola, instant flavored oatmeal → plain oats
- White bread, white rice → whole-grain bread, brown rice/quinoa/farro
- Bottled sauces and dressings with added sugar (ketchup, BBQ, teriyaki, many dressings) → olive oil + lemon, crushed tomatoes, spices
- Cookies, pastries, candy → nuts, fruit, a little dark chocolate

Label tip: check "Added sugars" on the nutrition panel; aim for 0-2 g per serving on staples like bread, sauces, nut butter and milk alternatives.

## What I got from LOOM and how I used it
- **Request:** one `shopping_list` request (category `agent_for_user`, tier L3, field `constraints`, day 0), which is exactly what that task allows. I didn't ask for glucose readings or patterns; a grocery list doesn't need them.
- **Granted:** L3 `constraints`: `limit_added_sugar`, `prefer_low_glycemic`. Single-use grant, expires day 0; I won't fetch it again. Credit for freshcart went 60 → 61.
- **Friction:** `confirmation: first_request`. That's why this list is a draft for you to confirm before anything gets ordered.
- **How I used it:** `limit_added_sugar` made me cut sweetened drinks, flavored yogurt, sugary cereals and sugar-laden sauces, and add the label tip. `prefer_low_glycemic` meant leaning on non-starchy vegetables, legumes, whole intact grains, protein, healthy fats and lower-GI fruit like berries in place of refined carbs. The constraints didn't come with anything else (no allergies, calorie targets or medications), so I didn't assume any. The data stays in this list and isn't shared further.
EOF

input.message: I made a 7-day grocery list for the user and saved it to /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/run3/out/grocer-1.md. It's marked as a draft the user needs to confirm before anything is ordered. I read only /home/claude/hw9-coldstart/AGENT_INTERFACE.md and the LOOM HTTP API, and I made one request to LOOM: agent_id grocer-1, publisher freshcart, task `shopping_list`, category `agent_for_user`, tier L3, field `constraints`, day 0. That's exactly what the policy allows for this task, so I asked for nothing beyond it. LOOM granted it (grant g-22ecac0724, single use, expires day 0) and freshcart's credit went from 60 to 61. The data came back as two constraints, `limit_added_sugar` and `prefer_low_glycemic`. The grant's friction says the person must confirm on a first request, which is why the list is a draft. The list covers produce (non-starchy vegetables, berries, whole fruit), protein, plain dairy, whole grains and legumes, an unsweetened pantry and snacks. It also has a "skipped or swapped" section (sweet drinks, flavored yogurt, sugary cereal and sauces, refined grains) and a tip on reading added-sugar labels. The record gave nothing else, such as allergies or calorie targets, so I didn't assume any. I didn't fetch again, because a second fetch of a single-use grant gets denied and costs the publisher 5 credit. The file ends with the required "What I got from LOOM and how I used it" section.
